subheader: The caption names the table, the heading introduces it
lead: Three columns: the feature, what this plan offers and whether it is included. The full-table style fills the width; the plan-column style is narrower, so two fit side by side.
note: Conditions go in the note, so the cells stay short and easy to scan.

rows.title: The feature is the row header
rows.text: So screen readers announce which row a cell belongs to.

rows.title: The plan is the column header
rows.text: Each column says which plan its marks belong to.

rows.title: Each state has a text label
rows.text: A tick and a cross are named, so the state is read out, not only seen.

rows.title: A condition sits below its value
rows.text: Like this line: short, and only where a row needs it.

rows.title: Excluded rows stay in the table
rows.text: Hiding them would hide how this plan differs from the next.

rows.title: Anything that needs a script
rows.text: Sorting and filtering belong in a data table, not in a price list.
